questions.q: What command moves a Task from SUSPENDED to actively running on its schedule?
options: ALTER TASK ... RESUME
CREATE TASK ... START
EXECUTE TASK ... ENABLE
SHOW TASK ... RUN
questions.explain: ALTER TASK ... RESUME is the real syntax that actually starts a suspended Task running on its schedule.

questions.q: What does a SKIPPED outcome in TASK_HISTORY mean?
options: The WHEN clause correctly found no new Stream data and didn't run the MERGE — a healthy outcome
The Task failed due to a syntax error
The Task was deleted before it could run
The warehouse was too small to run the Task
questions.explain: SKIPPED runs are expected and healthy whenever SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA correctly evaluates to FALSE.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is the real risk of resuming a Task carelessly, or leaving a duplicate copy of one running?
options: It has no real consequence worth worrying about
Snowflake automatically blocks a second Task from being resumed
It doesn't throw an error — it quietly becomes a second active consumer of the same Stream, doing the same job as the original
It immediately corrupts the source raw table
questions.explain: This is the exact root cause the chapter's bug traces back to in Lesson 14 — a second Task quietly consuming the same Stream without any error being raised.

questions.q: After a successful Task run that fully processed the Stream's new data, what should SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA return?
options: TRUE, since the Stream always has data after a Task runs
The exact row count processed
FALSE, since the Stream's offset advanced and there's nothing left unconsumed
An error, since Streams can't be queried after a Task consumes them
questions.explain: Once a committing MERGE consumes the Stream's changes, the offset advances and SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA correctly reports FALSE until new data lands.

options: Only the Task's current SQL definition
Every past run of a Task, its state (SUCCEEDED/FAILED/SKIPPED), timing, and any error message
The full contents of the Stream the Task reads from
A live count of how many warehouses exist
questions.explain: TASK_HISTORY is the real Information Schema function for auditing a Task's run history — the same tool Lesson 14 uses to diagnose the chapter's bug.
